issues.title: Terminology: two kinds of context need separate terms
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
## Problem

"Dialog Context" is used for the context the agent builds, which ACP
does not transmit. But ACP also carries information about the dialog
beyond its identifier, such as its lifecycle state, version, creator,
negotiated modalities, and lifetime. That information has no name.

## Proposal

```
Dialog Context:
: The information that ACP carries to correlate and maintain an
  agentic dialog, such as the Agentic Dialog Identifier, the lifecycle
  state, the participant that created the dialog, the negotiated
  modalities, and the lifetime.

Task Context:
: The context an agent builds and maintains over an agentic dialog,
  such as conversation history, instructions, and intermediate
  results. ACP does not transmit or interpret it.
```

Section 4.2.9 would then read "ACP doesn't Transmit Task Context".

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I cleanly separated this now, but used "dialog context" and "LLM context".

issues.title: Two-party model in Section 5 conflicts with other sections
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
## Problem

The draft describes the dialog topology in four inconsistent ways:

- Section 5: "fundamentally two-party"; topologies are built from
  "two unrelated instances of ACP ... connected only through delegated
  identities".
- Section 6.1.1: the ADID correlates messages "at every hop", is used
  by intermediaries, and "a dialog can involve more than two
  participants".
- Section 8.4: group communication with membership that changes during
  an exchange.
- Section 11: identifiers "persist across intermediaries and trust
  boundaries", which Section 5's model rules out.

## Proposal

Support both models, and state it once in Section 5:

```
A participant can carry a dialog to the next hop, or create a new
dialog, with a new dialog context, linked to the one it received. A
new dialog is created at a trust boundary and wherever local policy
requires it. Only the participant that creates the new dialog knows
the link. A dialog can have more than two participants, such as
members of a group.
```

Then align Section 11: a dialog context identifier does not cross a
trust boundary.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I've cleaned this up so it is clear that its 2-party, but that the ADID and principal identities are propagated into downstream agentic dialogs. I added a diagram as well to clarify this.

issues.title: Authorized agent
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: Section 6.1.2: who is "an authorized agent" here? It is not defined.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: Removed the word "authorized". It is not needed for this sentence to be understood anyway.

issues.title: Resumption: verify the resuming party and handle interrupted operations
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
Section 6.1.2 says an authorized agent uses the ADID to re-associate
with the dialog. Holding the ADID is not enough. On resumption, the
receiver should verify that the resuming party is the one whose
exchange was interrupted, that its dialog context is current, and that
the dialog is still authorized.

Also, resuming the dialog does not show whether an interrupted
operation completed. Its outcome stays unresolved until it can be
established, and resuming alone does not justify sending it again.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
Added: Of course, proper authentication is also required - knowledge of the ADID is insufficient for the newly formed connection to be associated to the agentic dialog. 

Also added: Resumption also requires protocol agreement on whether the client needs to reply prior input, or whether the server had already processed it.

issues.title: Should dialog identifiers be resistant to forgery?
issues.author: maxpassion
issues.body:
During the BoF discussion, the concern was raised that identifiers are too easy to forge.

Is there a need for identifiers to be verifiable, so that the party receiving an identifier can tell whether it belongs to the dialog it claims to represent?

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
I don't think this is complex. a dialog identifier should be a UUID, unique in space and time, and unguessable. Knowledge of an ADID provides no information whatsoever about the agentic dialog. KNowledge of he ADID is also insufficient for a client to connect to the server, and access the agentic dialog in any way - the client must also authenticate itself, and be authorized for such access. 

I've added this to the doc.

issues.title: Distinguish a failed check from one that could not be completed
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
Section 6.1.2 lists lifecycle events but not the states they move between, so it cannot say, for example, that a terminated dialog
cannot be resumed. Lifecycle states and transitions are being discussed for draft-zahed-agentproto-refarch:
https://github.com/zaheduzzaman/overall-aiproto-architecture/pull/8

Cancellation of prior input is a task-level action, already covered in Section 6.1.6, and rehydration is a client synchronizing its local
storage. Neither changes the state of the dialog, so they do not belong in the lifecycle list.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I think the actual state machine is outside the scope of this doc and would belong in the actual protocol spec. I did clarify that terminated means it cannot be resumed.

issues.title: Add an operational flow
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
The draft describes each function separately but does not show how
they combine in one interaction, from selecting an agent to completing
the task. An operational flow covering connection, authentication,
authorization, dialog creation, delegation, continuity, and completion
is being added to draft-zahed-agentproto-refarch:
https://github.com/zaheduzzaman/overall-aiproto-architecture/pull/7

Suggest including it here.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I think this is too low level and belongs in the protocol doc.

issues.title: Resuming does not establish the outcome of an interrupted operation
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
Section 6.1.4 describes a server failing while processing a request,
but not what the client does after resuming the dialog.

For example, the client asks an agent to book a room, and the
connection drops before the reply arrives. After resuming, the client
cannot tell whether the room was booked. Sending the request again
could book a second room. The client should first find out whether
the request completed.

See Section 4.2 of draft-agentic-ai-usecases-requirements:
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-agentic-ai-usecases-requirements/

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
I added:

* Resumption: Resuming input or output, requiring (if needed) creation or modification of transport connections to convey the input or output. Resumption also requires protocol agreement on whether the client needs to replay prior input, or whether the server had already processed it.

issues.title: Bring back the end-to-end architecture diagram
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
The end-to-end architecture diagram from draft-zahed-agentproto-refarch was dropped. It showed users, agents, and tools over the agent
communication protocol, with its dialog, authorization and delegation, and identity management blocks, running over the transport and
security layers. The current figures show the network topology and the functional blocks separately, but not how ACP relates to transport and
security. Suggest bringing it back.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I brought back a simplified version of it into the section on interaction patterns.

issues.title: Multi-level identification
issues.author: khyao78
issues.body:
In the discussion yesterday, we tentatively agreed that a dialog refers to the conversation between two parties, while the dialog context is protocol-level metadata used to correlate multiple dialogs.

Then, regarding identification, do we need multi-level identifiers? Identifying both the dialog (dialog identifier) and the dialog context (dialog context identifier)?

The two identifiers serve different functions.

The dialog ID represents the independence of each dialog.

The dialog context ID is used for logical association/binding across multiple dialogs and can serve as the identifier for the complete envelope.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: We don't need two. I hope this is now clear in the document, there is a diagram on how delegation works.
